text:
tom: Hey all, first day here. VPN (WireGuard) connects fine but our internal build system (build.redwood.internal) fails from my laptop with weird "connection refused" errors even though the hostname resolves. Browser can reach the CI UI. Anyone seen hostnames resolving but sockets failing?
it-support: Welcome Tom! Quick Q: do DNS records for that host include AAAA (IPv6) entries? Some ISPs give you IPv6 connectivity that doesn't properly route to our internal IPv6, causing clients to try IPv6 first and fail.
tom: I just did `dig build.redwood.internal A AAAA +short` and it returned both 10.240.5.12 and 2601:abcd::12 (AAAA). I don't think our infra announces IPv6 to customers yet.
nora: Yep, that explains it. Many libc/resolver stacks prefer IPv6 when both A and AAAA exist. If your machine chooses the IPv6 address but there's no route via the VPN for it, the TCP handshake times out quickly. Browser may fall back to IPv4 or use a different stack.
ops: Quick workarounds: 1) force IPv4 in CLI with curl/git by using `-4` or `GIT_SSH_COMMAND='ssh -4'`, 2) disable IPv6 temporarily on the client, or 3) add a host-specific /etc/hosts entry pointing the host to its IPv4 address so the system never sees the AAAA.
nora: Example commands:```bash
# temporary curl/test using IPv4
curl -4 -v https://build.redwood.internal:8443/
# add hosts entry (sudo)
echo "10.240.5.12 build.redwood.internal" | sudo tee -a /etc/hosts
# disable IPv6 until reboot (Linux)
sudo sysctl -w net.ipv6.conf.all.disable_ipv6=1
```
tom: I tried `curl -4` and that connects. Can we make this less manual for other new-hires?
it-support: We'll add two things to onboarding: a short note about AAAA records and two recommended quick fixes (prefer IPv4 with CLI flags or temporary /etc/hosts entry). Ops also suggested we filter AAAA records on the resolver we push via VPN until infra fully supports IPv6.
ops: On our side we should also make sure internal DNS only returns A for internal-only services, or announce a proper IPv6 route if we enable IPv6. For now we can patch the internal DNS zone to remove AAAA for hostnames that aren't routable. I can file a ticket.
tom: One more issue: git over SSH still tried IPv6 despite hosts file and `ssh -4` worked. How do I make git use ssh -4 by default?
nora: Add to ~/.ssh/config:
```text
Host *.redwood.internal
  AddressFamily inet
```
That forces SSH to IPv4 for those hosts. Or set `GIT_SSH_COMMAND="ssh -4"` in your environment for that repo.
tom: Added the ssh config, git clone works now. Thanks!
infra-bot: Internal doc: https://confluence.redwood/infra/ipv6-split-tunnel-notes (guidance for new-hires) :white_check_mark:
tom: Thanks everyone. I'll paste the dig output (redacted) and the exact hosts line I used into the onboarding checklist so other IPv6-enabled home networks don't get stuck.
it-support: Great, welcome aboard and congrats on day 1!"
